intent_snapshot.goal: Deliver S2 of Initiative batch-resource-safety after S1, per docs/specs/batch-resource-safety-s2.spec.md and user-approved option A: retain Executor Lanes and unknown ignored files, block destructive redo without trustworthy exit evidence, and report retained resources across completion/restart. Automatic lifecycle restoration is explicitly deferred; no new session-management subsystem is included.

acceptance.assertion: Per user-approved option A and D1/D3 in docs/specs/batch-resource-safety-s2.spec.md: current Hosts provide no trusted Executor exit proof, so integrated Lanes and all their files remain intact for live, unknown, idle or done sessions, including unknown ignored sentinels and no-active-claim cases. Positive: ordinary creation, integration and passing final verification still complete with a retained Lane. Bound: user-provided Lanes remain untouched and detached Parent verification cleanup is not confused with Executor cleanup. Agreed seams: tests/batch-parent-branch.test.ts, tests/unattended-batch-lanes.test.ts.

Per D2 in docs/specs/batch-resource-safety-s2.spec.md: conflict redo, persisted redo-grant resume, parked revival and missing-path recovery refuse destructive Lane recreation without trusted exit evidence, preserving refs, worktree registrations, ignored bytes and prior delivery reachability. Positive: independent siblings continue. Bound: repeated ticks or confirmation do not spend additional grants for the same refusal, delete a branch, or duplicate integration. Agreed seams: tests/batch-merge-queue.test.ts, tests/batch-parked-revive.test.ts, tests/batch-redo-slot.test.ts.

Per D4 in docs/specs/batch-resource-safety-s2.spec.md: ordinary, terminal replay and completedParentReport outputs identify retained Lane task/path and missing-exit-evidence reason while preserving delivery completion and audit identity. Negative: repeated terminal reporting cannot drop cleanup notices, reenroll completed children, or claim a present Lane released. Bound: external path disappearance is observation only and never authorizes automatic redo. Agreed seams: tests/batch-final-report.test.ts, tests/goal-driven-batch-run.test.ts.

Per D5 in docs/specs/batch-resource-safety-s2.spec.md: affected runtime/packaged Lane lifecycle instructions consistently describe conservative retention and paused destructive redo, with the named restoration owner, capability milestone and exit conditions. Negative: Git-clean or Kernel-terminal alone is not described as permitting automatic Lane deletion. Bound: existing legacy ownership and user-dialog protections remain; maintained prompt mirrors agree. Agreed seams: tests/role-prompt-bridge.test.ts, tests/dist-docs-sync-contract.test.ts.

intent_snapshot.scope_size_reason: One fail-closed Lane resource-lifecycle invariant spans release, redo/revival and terminal replay; its focused behavioral tests, source/mirror contracts and ADR must ship together so no destructive alternate path or contradictory cleanup promise remains. No new Host process subsystem or persistent schema is added.

attestations.summary: Provenance verified (commit 33b4d36 has single parent 9f1aff1, tree 1c08186). Runtime removes all Lane delete/recreate paths, parks conflict, redo-grant, revival and missing-path cases with batch_lane_redo_retained without spending grants, and reports batch_lane_retained in ordinary, terminal-replay and completedParentReport outputs. Docs and prompt mirrors agree, and the seam tests cover AC1-AC4.

advisory_findings.summary: deriveChildRedoEnrollment and deriveParkedChildRedoEnrollment in batch_kernel_port.ts no longer have a production caller (batch_lanes.ts dropped its imports) but are still exported and only tests call them. They are a dormant grant-spending path that the restoration proposal should remove or re-gate.

evidence.trigger: A future caller imports the still-exported deriveChildRedoEnrollment → it spends a redo grant even though no Lane recreation is allowed. No current production path reaches it, so there is no observable wrong result today.

findings.summary: AC3 names tests/batch-final-report.test.ts and tests/goal-driven-batch-run.test.ts as its agreed seams, but neither file changed. The retained-Lane report behavior and SCN-6 (a reopened completed report still identifies retained Lanes and does not claim cleanup or re-enroll the child) are asserted only in tests/unattended-batch-lanes.test.ts, so the agreed seams were replaced without saying so.

evidence.trigger: At revision e64c0bb, AC3's agreed seam files contain no assertion on batch_lane_retained, lane_refusals, completedParentReport or retained-Lane next_action (a grep finds no match in either file). A regression in how retainedLaneNotices or retainedLaneAction feed completedParentReport, a terminal replay or an ordinary report would therefore pass both agreed seams. AC3's bound (an already absent integrated Lane path is only observed as released and never authorizes a redo) is also not pinned for an integrated Lane at any seam.
